Red pandas are found in the Eastern Himalayas and surrounding high-altitude regions of Asia [d1][d6]. Their range spans Nepal, India, Bhutan, Myanmar (Burma), and China — particularly the west Sichuan and Yunnan Provinces — as well as Tibet [d2][d4][d5]. They inhabit temperate broadleaved forests with bamboo understories, typically at altitudes between 2,400 and 3,900 meters (above 4,000 feet) [d7][d9]. Almost 50% of their habitat is concentrated in the Eastern Himalayas, and they spend the vast majority of their lives in trees [d6][d5]. Two distinct populations exist: the Himalayan red panda (found mainly in Nepal, India, and Bhutan) and the Chinese red panda (found primarily in China and Myanmar), separated by the Siang River boundary [d3][d7].
